items.question: What is the never-exceed airspeed (Vne) at 2200 lb takeoff gross weight and below?
items.explanation: Section 2 AIRSPEED LIMITS specifies Vne 130 KIAS at 2200 lb TOGW and below.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: AIRSPEED LIMITS (p.2-1)

items.question: What is the never-exceed airspeed (Vne) when takeoff gross weight is over 2200 lb?
items.explanation: For TOGW over 2200 lb the POH limits Vne to 120 KIAS.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: AIRSPEED LIMITS (p.2-1)

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed in autorotation?
items.explanation: The AIRSPEED LIMITS table gives a maximum autorotation airspeed of 100 KIAS.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: AIRSPEED LIMITS (p.2-1)

items.question: With any combination of cabin doors removed, what is the maximum approved airspeed?
items.explanation: Additional airspeed limits specify 100 KIAS maximum with any combination of cabin doors removed.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: AIRSPEED LIMITS (p.2-1)

items.question: For power-on operation, what is the permitted main rotor speed range?
items.explanation: ROTOR SPEED LIMITS list a power-on rotor speed range of 101-102% NR (404-408 RPM).
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: ROTOR SPEED LIMITS (p.2-2)

items.question: For power-off rotor operation, what is the permitted rotor speed range?
items.explanation: With power off, rotor speed is limited to 90-108% NR (360-432 RPM).
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: ROTOR SPEED LIMITS (p.2-2)

items.question: When is transient operation below 101% rotor RPM permitted?
options: Only in autorotation below 500 ft AGL
items.explanation: A note under rotor speed limits allows transient operation below 101% NR only for emergency procedures training.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: ROTOR SPEED LIMITS (p.2-2)

items.question: What is the maximum continuous engine speed for the IO-540-AE1A5, expressed as a percentage of rated RPM?
items.explanation: POWERPLANT LIMITATIONS show maximum continuous engine speed of 102% (2718 RPM).
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: POWERPLANT LIMITATIONS (p.2-2)

items.question: Which combination of gross weight limits is correct for the R44 II?
items.explanation: WEIGHT LIMITS define a maximum gross weight of 2500 lb and a minimum gross weight of 1600 lb.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: WEIGHT LIMITS (p.2-3)

items.question: What is the maximum permitted weight per seat, including baggage compartment?
items.explanation: The WEIGHT LIMITS section states a maximum of 300 lb (136 kg) per seat including baggage compartment.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: WEIGHT LIMITS (p.2-3)

items.question: What is the maximum allowable load in any baggage compartment?
items.explanation: Maximum load in any baggage compartment is limited to 50 lb (23 kg).
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: WEIGHT LIMITS (p.2-3)

items.question: With all doors installed, what minimum solo pilot weight ensures the center of gravity will be within limits without adding ballast?
items.explanation: CENTER OF GRAVITY LIMITS note that a solo pilot weight of 150 lb (68 kg) or more keeps CG within limits with doors installed.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: CENTER OF GRAVITY LIMITS (p.2-3)

items.question: Are aerobatic manoeuvres permitted in the R44 II?
options: Only for training with an instructor on board
items.explanation: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS state that aerobatic flight is prohibited.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS (p.2-5)

items.question: Which manoeuvre is specifically prohibited because of the risk of catastrophic loss of lateral control in low-G conditions?
items.explanation: The FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS section specifically prohibits low-G cyclic pushovers due to loss of lateral control risk.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS (p.2-5)

items.question: According to the limitations, is flight in known icing conditions permitted?
options: Yes, if pitot heat is ON
No, flight in known icing conditions is prohibited
items.explanation: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS state that flight in known icing conditions is prohibited.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS (p.2-5)

items.question: Which combination of altitude limitations is correct for the R44 II?
options: Maximum operating density altitude 12,000 ft; maximum operating altitude 8,000 ft AGL
Maximum operating density altitude 14,000 ft; maximum operating altitude 9,000 ft AGL
Maximum operating density altitude 16,000 ft; maximum operating altitude 10,000 ft AGL
Maximum operating density altitude 10,000 ft; maximum operating altitude 14,000 ft AGL
items.explanation: The POH limits operation to a maximum density altitude of 14,000 ft and a maximum operating altitude of 9,000 ft AGL.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS (p.2-5)

items.question: Which kinds of operation are approved for the R44 II under the POH?
options: Day and night VFR and IFR
items.explanation: KINDS OF OPERATION LIMITATIONS approve the R44 II for day and night VFR operations.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: KINDS OF OPERATION LIMITATIONS (p.2-6)

items.question: For solo flight, where must the pilot be seated according to the flight crew limitations?
items.explanation: Minimum flight crew is one pilot in the right front seat; solo flight is from the right front seat.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: FLIGHT CREW LIMITATIONS (p.2-5)

items.question: Which group of systems must be operational for dispatch according to the limitations?
options: Alternator, RPM governor, low rotor RPM warning system, OAT gage, and hydraulic control system
Alternator, pitot heat, GPS, and autopilot
Hydraulic system, anti-ice system, and flight director only
Only the rotor brake and low fuel warning system
items.explanation: The FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS list the alternator, RPM governor, low rotor RPM warning system, OAT gage, and hydraulic control system as required for dispatch.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS (p.2-5)

items.question: With fuel tanks equipped with bladders, what is the combined usable fuel capacity?
items.explanation: FUEL LIMITATIONS state that with bladder tanks usable capacity is 29.5 and 17.0 US gal, for a combined usable fuel of 46.5 US gal (176 liters).
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: FUEL LIMITATIONS (p.2-6)
